importantFindings.title: One malformed stored birth date (a legacy 0.2.0 value) makes Allievi, Equipaggi and Comandate unavailable, and the edit form's own repair path is unreachable
importantFindings.evidence: Repro on a dev server, Pixel 7 emulation: seed the 0.2.0 fixture with seedV020Fixture (src/test/v020MigrationHarness.ts), then UPDATE students SET dateOfBirth = <value> for one student and open each area from Home. For each of "2000-02-30", "0002-03-12", "20000-03-12" and "12/03/2000": Allievi, Equipaggi and Comandate each show 'non disponibili - Non riesco a leggere l'archivio locale. Riprova'; Valutazioni, Volontari and Barche still open. Cause: readValidStudents (src/features/students/StudentManagement.tsx:157) throws on any validateStudentRecords issue (src/domain/invariants.ts:177, code invalid-student-date-of-birth); the same gate is inside readValidCrewState (readValidCrewState, CrewManagement.tsx:1138 at HEAD) and readValidDutyData (DutyManagement.tsx:227). The form's F2R-3 fallback (hadInvalidStoredDate, StudentManagement.tsx:481) can only be reached from the list that the gate blocks, so it is dead in practice. A value with surrounding whitespace (" 2000-03-12") passes the checker (it trims, invariants.ts:177) but calculateAge/parseDateOnly (src/domain/student.ts:15, :254) throw on the untrimmed string: Allievi then falls into ScreenErrorBoundary ('Questa schermata non si è aperta') and repeats after 'Torna alla Home'. 0.2.0 autosaved a native date input that only had a max attribute (git show v0.2.0:src/features/students/StudentManagement.tsx, near line 504; no validity check), so a half-typed year such as 0002 or 20000 could have been stored. Age arithmetic itself is correct at every boundary I tried (birthday on the first day = adult, day before/after, 29 Feb on 28 Feb/1 Mar, 17/18).
importantFindings.impact: No row is lost or changed, but a single malformed legacy row disables three core areas with no way to repair it in the app; the only exit is Impostazioni > Elimina il corso. Likelihood is low (0.3.0 is the first version on a phone, so 0.2.0 data exists mostly on development machines), but the CHANGELOG sentence 'A 0.1.0 or 0.2.0 course opens unchanged' is only true for well-formed rows, and the screen blames the local storage when the cause is one record.
importantFindings.suggestedFix: Do not make an unreadable birth date fatal. Either normalise it at the read boundary (listStudents returns dateOfBirth '' for a value that is not a real date, which the form already treats as 'age to complete') and drop invalid-student-date-of-birth from the fail-closed set, or keep the gate but let the Allievi list open and mark the student 'età da completare'. Make the checker and calculateAge agree on trimming. Add one E2E that seeds a malformed date into the 0.2.0 fixture and repairs it through the UI. Show the failing record or check code on the 'non disponibile' screens.

importantFindings.title: A fault whose updatedAt precedes its createdAt, which the app itself writes after a backwards clock change, makes Avarie, Barche and Equipaggi unavailable with no in-app repair
importantFindings.evidence: Repro: seed the 0.2.0 fixture, UPDATE faults SET updatedAt = createdAt minus 60 s for one fault, open each area. Avarie, Barche and Equipaggi show 'non disponibili - Non riesco a leggere l'archivio locale'; Comandate, Valutazioni and Allievi still open. The app writes this state itself: createFault, updateFaultState and updateFaultDescription stamp new Date().toISOString() (src/persistence/boats.ts:215, :244, :258) and validateBoatRecords flags updatedAt < createdAt as invalid-fault-chronology (src/domain/invariants.ts:320); validateBoatRecords is applied by the Barche load (BoatManagement.tsx:77), the Avarie load (FaultManagement.tsx:27) and readValidCrewState (CrewManagement.tsx, line 1181 at HEAD). The only way to rewrite updatedAt is to edit the fault from the Avarie page, which is the blocked page.
importantFindings.impact: Needs the device clock to step back between creating a fault and a later edit (a manual time fix, a phone that had a wrong date and then syncs, an NTP step within seconds of creating then immediately editing). Rare, but the consequence is three areas bricked mid-course on the water, for a rule the checker could not use to protect anything (chronology is not read by any feature).
importantFindings.suggestedFix: Write updatedAt = max(now, createdAt) in the three fault writers, and take invalid-fault-chronology out of the fail-closed read gate (keep it as an advisory in verify:domain). Add a persistence test that edits a fault with a clock mocked earlier than createdAt.

importantFindings.title: saveDutyPlan does not check that assigned students exist, unlike saveCrewPlan and saveEvaluation; a stale second instance can write a duty for a deleted student and brick Equipaggi and Comandate
importantFindings.evidence: Repro at the persistence boundary (the same call a stale Comandate page makes): on the 0.2.0 fixture, saveDutyPlan('course-v020-d2', [...assignments, {dayId:'wednesday', studentId:'student-that-was-deleted'}], settings) is ACCEPTED, while saveCrewPlan with the same unknown student is rejected ('Crew student does not belong to course') and saveEvaluation is rejected ('Evaluation student does not belong to course'). Afterwards Equipaggi and Comandate show 'non disponibili' (validateDutyRecords: dangling-duty-student, invariants.ts) and the Comandate page that could remove the row is the blocked page. src/persistence/duties.ts:126-258 validates day ids and duplicates only; settings.stayOverStudentIds is not checked either. A student with no references can be deleted (deleteUnusedStudent), and a second instance keeps its old student list: two tabs are possible on the phone (Chromium with an Android user agent opened a second tab to Home in 0.4 s and wrote 60 interleaved rows with integrity_check ok).
importantFindings.impact: Needs one instance to delete a student that another instance's Comandate page still lists, then save. Low likelihood, high consequence, and it is the only write path that can create a dangling reference the invariant checker (and the UI gate) will reject.
importantFindings.suggestedFix: In saveDutyPlan's transaction, load the course's student ids and reject any assignment or stay-over id outside them, exactly as saveCrewPlan does; add the case to src/persistence/duties.test.ts. Optionally let the read gate drop (not fail on) assignments of missing students.

importantFindings.title: The course's start date, ISO week and label are derived only from the day the course is created, so creating it on a weekday of a running course stores next week's Saturday, and nothing lets the operator correct it
importantFindings.evidence: src/App.tsx:284 calls buildCourseDetails(family, level, today) and src/domain/course.ts:45-64 returns the Saturday of today's ISO week. Run with the real function: created Sat 29 Aug or Sun 30 Aug 2026 gives D2 35, start 2026-08-29 (right); created Mon 31 Aug to Fri 4 Sep gives D2 36, start 2026-09-05; created Wed 9 Sep gives D2 37, start 2026-09-12. A course that began on 29 Aug and is set up on the Tuesday is therefore stored as week 36 starting a week late. Everything keyed on startDate follows: ages worked out from a stored or scanned birth date (calculateStudentAge, scan review), minor status, the default evaluation session.
importantFindings.impact: A wrong, uneditable course identity and an age-at-first-day that can be off by one year for a student whose birthday falls in the shifted week, which flips the minor/adult badge that drives duty balancing and crew warnings. Typed ages (the default mode since F2) are unaffected. This matches the spec as written ('derives... from the date'), so it is a semantic gap rather than a defect.
importantFindings.suggestedFix: Let the operator confirm or pick the first Saturday on the creation screen (preview already shows the range), or derive from the most recent Saturday when created Monday to Friday; record the choice in 04_IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md. At minimum list it under Known limitations in CHANGELOG.md.

importantFindings.title: The course exists only in browser storage that the app never asks to keep (no navigator.storage.persist) and cannot export
importantFindings.evidence: grep for storage.persist / StorageManager in src finds nothing; docs/post-mvp/1_0_0_NEXT_STEPS.md plans it for 0.4.0. The CHANGELOG already warns about uninstalling or clearing data but not about the browser evicting a non-persistent origin under storage pressure or, on Safari, after seven days without use in a non-installed tab. Erase works (see inspected evidence), so the only loss paths are outside the app's control.
importantFindings.impact: A week of students, crews, duties and evaluations has a single copy. Chrome grants installed PWAs durable storage heuristically; an instructor using a plain browser tab, or iOS Safari outside the home screen, has no such guarantee. Already disclosed and scheduled, so not a blocker.
importantFindings.suggestedFix: Call navigator.storage.persist() once after the course is created (local, no network, three lines) and say in Known limitations that the course should be used from the installed app. Export remains the 0.4.0 item.

qolFindings.title: The age field autosaves a half-typed number and drops the stored birth date the moment it differs
qolFindings.evidence: src/features/students/StudentManagement.tsx:481-560 and :643 (500 ms debounce). Repro on the 0.2.0 fixture, Davide (stored date, age 31): select the age and type '3', wait 0.9 s: row becomes dateOfBirth '' and declaredAgeAtCourseStart 3 (a 3-year-old, flagged Minorenne); typing '2' makes it 32; retyping the original 31 restores the stored date only because the form still holds the original student prop. Accepted range is 0-120 (parsedDeclaredAge, MAX_DECLARED_STUDENT_AGE).
qolFindings.impact: A pause mid-number, or leaving the form at that moment, commits an implausible age and discards the original date; the owner decided age-only, so only the transient value is the problem. Minor/adult drives duty balancing.
qolFindings.suggestedFix: Commit the age on blur or on Fine/Back, or hold the autosave while the number is under a plausible floor (for example under 5 for a course student) and ask before replacing a stored date.

qolFindings.title: createFault checks the boat and inserts in two separate steps
qolFindings.evidence: src/persistence/boats.ts:206-236: getOptional boat then db.execute INSERT, not one transaction, unlike deleteBoat (boats.ts:170) which checks references inside a transaction. A deleteBoat that commits between the two leaves a fault pointing at a missing boat, and listFaults then throws for every caller (boats.ts:79 'Fault references missing boat', not scoped by course).
qolFindings.impact: Window of milliseconds and needs two actors on the same boat, so practically unreachable; the consequence would be Avarie, Barche and Equipaggi unavailable.
qolFindings.suggestedFix: Run the existence check and the insert inside db.writeTransaction.

qolFindings.title: The OCR worker is kept alive after a scan and holds the last roster image and recognition result in memory, including after Erase course
qolFindings.evidence: src/capabilities/studentScan.ts:1254-1285: workerPromise is a module singleton, never terminated; recognize() is the only use. Nothing is persisted (IndexedDB audit after a full scan: no PNG or JPEG signature in cvc-helper.db blocks, only the OCR language file in keyval-store; no img or canvas left in the DOM after saving), and Erase course clears every table, but the WASM heap of a live worker still holds the pixels and text until the app process ends.
qolFindings.impact: In-memory only, on the owner's own device; but the roster photo is the most sensitive item and an installed PWA can live for days.
qolFindings.suggestedFix: worker.terminate() after the review is built (or after an idle minute) and in eraseAllCourseData; the next scan recreates it from the local cache.

qolFindings.title: Two open instances of the app overwrite each other's whole-session plans without a warning
qolFindings.evidence: saveCrewPlan (src/persistence/crews.ts:311-672) replaces the full session from the caller's in-memory plan (CrewManagement commit, line 1652 at HEAD). Repro at the persistence boundary on the 0.2.0 fixture: tab B moves one student to A terra, then stale tab A moves a different student; the final state shows tab B's move undone (davide back in his crew) with no error. Database-level concurrency is safe: two tabs wrote 30 rows each interleaved, 63 rows seen by both and by a fresh tab, PRAGMA integrity_check ok, in Android-UA and desktop modes. PowerSync only logs 'Multiple tab support is not enabled' to the console on Android/iOS (resolveAndValidateOptions.js:23).
qolFindings.impact: Lost update, never an invariant violation: the saved plan is always self-consistent. Out of scope for 0.3.0 (no multi-editor), noted so the 0.4.0 data work starts from it.
qolFindings.suggestedFix: Optional: a navigator.locks guard that shows 'App già aperta in un'altra scheda' in the second instance.

qolFindings.title: No automated tripwire for personal-data patterns in tracked files
qolFindings.evidence: scripts/check-repository.mjs checks data/private/ is untracked and absolute machine paths (about line 246) but nothing for phone-like numbers, birth dates or e-mail addresses. My scan of the 727 tracked files found: 79 phone-like numbers, 63 of them obvious placeholders and the other 16 in invented contexts (fixture and test rows, the M0 spike archive); no e-mail address; birth-date-shaped strings only beside invented names in .evidence review notes, tests, mock.js and the synthetic corpus generator; the 7 evidence screenshots I opened (scan editor and review, age review, student list, crew summary) and the two fixture images I opened (ocr-sheet-clear, one synthetic sheet) show invented people ('dati inventati' printed on the synthetic sheet). So the tree is clean today, but it stays clean by habit.
qolFindings.impact: The 2026-09 incident (real data in published history) was found by a one-off scan; a future pasted roster line would be caught by nobody.
qolFindings.suggestedFix: Add a check:repository rule that fails on a phone-like number or dd/mm/yyyy date outside an explicit allow-list file of the known invented values.

qolFindings.title: Residual traces the app cannot erase are not mentioned: the clipboard image and error messages that carry a stored value
qolFindings.evidence: Copia immagine puts a PNG with the crew or Comandate names on the OS clipboard (src/lib/summaryShare.ts copyImageToClipboard); Erase course (src/persistence/courses.ts:75) cannot clear it. The summary PNG itself is in memory only (SummaryImageButton refs; the __CVC_TEST__ hook is gated by import.meta.env.DEV and is absent from a production build, checked with grep over a scratch vite build). calculateAge throws 'Invalid date-only value: <stored value>' (student.ts:17) and React logs a caught render error to the console, so a corrupt stored birth date appears in the device console; the app's own console.error calls (CrewManagement.tsx:1323 and 1338 at HEAD) print identifiers only.
qolFindings.impact: Local to the owner's device; no network path (below).
qolFindings.suggestedFix: One sentence in the Erase confirmation and in Known limitations about the clipboard; keep stored values out of thrown messages.

qolFindings.title: The 'non disponibile' screens give no cause
qolFindings.evidence: Every fail-closed screen (StudentManagement.tsx:1390, DutyManagement.tsx:1322, the crew and boat screens) shows 'Non riesco a leggere l'archivio locale. Riprova' for an invariant violation, which Riprova cannot fix (UG2-DAT-1 to UG2-DAT-3); the thrown message ('Persisted student state violates invariants') and the issue codes are only in the console.
qolFindings.impact: An operator on the water cannot tell storage failure from one bad record, or learn that erasing the course is the only fix.
qolFindings.suggestedFix: Show the first issue code and the record's display name (not the value) under the message, plus a plain sentence for the invariant case.

evidenceInspected: Read: AGENTS.md sections 10-13, 03_TECHNICAL_DECISIONS.md, the UG2/F1-F4 sections of 04_IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md, docs/post-mvp/0_3_0_QUESTIONS.md, docs/post-mvp/1_0_0_NEXT_STEPS.md, CHANGELOG.md, .evidence/UG2/*.json (migration, physical-device, synthetic roster), .evidence/F1/history-rewrite.json.

Source read: src/persistence/{db,courses,students,crews,boats,duties,evaluations,volunteers}.ts, src/domain/{invariants,student,crews,course,config}.ts, src/domain/studentMigration.ts, StudentManagement.tsx, StudentScan.tsx (commit path), CrewManagement.tsx (load, commit, copy, capacity), DutyManagement.tsx (load, persist), EvaluationManagement.tsx (save), CourseErase.tsx, summaryShare.ts, SummaryImageButton.tsx, speech.ts, studentScan.ts, vite.config.ts, @powersync/web option resolution (multi-tab, IDBBatchAtomicVFS exclusive locks).

Commit under review 990ee0a. The only change since 40b55c1 in src is the removal of formatCrewAnnouncement (dead code); src/persistence, src/domain/invariants.ts and src/domain/student.ts are identical in both. The working tree carried other agents' uncommitted layout edits in CrewManagement.tsx and DutyManagement.tsx and two untracked tests/e2e/zz-tmp-* specs; none was touched or relied on. The only repository file I wrote is this report.

Commands: npm run verify:domain (check:repository, check:domain, check:compatibility: PASS, 22 rows); npx vitest run src/persistence src/domain/invariants.test.ts src/domain/student.test.ts src/domain/crews.test.ts src/test (12 files, 177 tests, PASS); targeted Playwright on pixel-7-chrome: u02-migration (3), u02-deletion-integrity, ug2-upgraded-week (6 tests total PASS) and ug1-upgraded-week (1, PASS). Not run: verify:all, the other projects, ug2-hostile-roster.

Migration: the frozen src/test/v020Schema.ts matches the schema in git show v0.2.0:src/persistence/db.ts for all 13 tables; db.ts differs from the tag by exactly students.declaredAgeAtCourseStart and crews.capacity (both nullable); @powersync/web and wa-sqlite versions are unchanged since 0.2.0 (package.json/lock diff is the version bump and sharp only), so the storage format is the same. Local-only tables keep rows as JSON, so no destructive migration exists. Verified legacy crews: a 6-member flexible crew with no capacity reads as capacity 6 and keeps all six; a crew with null member positions reads packed with capacity 4; after removing the second member the seats become 0,2,3,4,5 and survive a reload; lowering capacity below the highest occupied seat is refused (and its button is disabled in the UI); whole-database invariants after these steps: zero issues.

Crew fuzz in a real browser (my own script, persistence plus domain functions): 1,925 random operations (move to a seat or a free slot, swap, remove, A terra, capacity +/-, add/remove crew, boat out/in, assign boat, copy previous session, Mezzi/unassigned) across D1, D2, D3 and C1 courses and three sessions, each saved through saveCrewPlan and read back through readCrewPlan: 0 save rejections, 0 read errors, 0 round-trip mismatches, 0 validateCourseState issues (checked every fifth step and at the end).

Atomicity: 20 abrupt page reloads started while saveCrewPlan was in flight (8 crews, 24 members, 8 boats, 6 A terra) ended in only two states, the old empty plan (1) or the whole new plan (19), integrity_check ok every time. Double-click on Salva volontario and Salva allievo created exactly one row each. Interleaved writes from two tabs: no error, no lost row, integrity ok.

Age rules (domain function): birthday on the first day -> adult; day before -> adult; day after -> minor; 29 Feb born on 28 Feb (17, minor) and 1 Mar (18); negative age for a birth date after the course start is not rejected (the checker does not receive startDate in validateStudentRecords).

Erase course: after the 0.2.0 fixture plus unique markers in a student note, surname, phone, volunteer, evaluation note and fault, the UI erase (Impostazioni, checkbox, Elimina tutto) leaves 0 rows in all 12 course tables (meta keeps its one number row), and a raw scan of every IndexedDB record finds none of the markers nor the names of the six students and three volunteers, before or after a reload (they were present in the blocks before). localStorage, sessionStorage, Cache Storage and OPFS hold nothing. COURSE_DATA_TABLES is pinned to db.ts by courses.test.ts:100-110.

Privacy: production build to a scratch directory (vite build, not npm run build, to keep dist/ untouched): no __CVC_TEST__, no fixture or corpus strings, no source maps; the only off-origin hosts in the bundle are huggingface.co (the pinned speech model on first use) and the unused cdn.jsdelivr.net default. Full journey on the production build (create course, gallery photo, crop, OCR, review, save, open Equipaggi) with every non-origin request aborted and logged: 0 external requests, 51 same-origin GETs, none with a body, window.__CVC_TEST__ undefined; no image bytes in IndexedDB; no img or canvas in the DOM after saving; the assistant prompt carries no personal data; no personal data in URLs, titles or history state (ids only). The speech path was not exercised (it downloads the model on first use by design).

Repository: git ls-files scanned for phone-like numbers, birth-date-like strings and e-mail addresses with values masked (counts and paths only; see UG2-DAT-10); data/private was neither opened nor listed; 7 evidence screenshots and 2 fixture images were viewed and show invented people (the other tracked images were not opened).

Probes behind the findings: malformed birth dates (six values) against all areas; fault with updatedAt before createdAt; saveDutyPlan, saveCrewPlan and saveEvaluation with a missing student; rapid age edits in the real form; stale whole-plan overwrite; course dates for eleven creation days.
